as they don't seem to be packaged anywhere they are probably irrelevant

@quantenzitrone - This will likely be annoying to parse out.  For instance, Basecalc.c version (https://www.softintegration.com/chhtml/toolkit/demos/X11/xlib/basecalc/basecalc.html) has "sublicense & sell" listed in the rights grant but no disclaimer.  

In the two versions where the disclaimer placement is either top (https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/fig2dev/pic2tpic.1.en.html) versus bottom (https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/xfig/xfig.1.en.html), the version with the disclaimer at the top also differs similarly with the "sublicense & sell" language +  includes this patent grant: _This license includes without limitation a license to do the foregoing actions under any patents of the party supplying this software to the X Consortium._

Comparing the Basecalc version to the disclaimer version that has sublicense/sell/patent grant language - there is a further difference from Basecalc which states "with the only requirement being that this copyright notice remain intact." 

These aren't items that can be solved by markup since they are substantive legal language.

I suggest we pick one, rule on that then have separate issues for subsequent identifiers that have minor name variations to indicate the differences.
